directive: Match the perceived accessibility of Legend of Mushroom's premium resources and frequent free-draw cadence, while combining the rapid reset and re-clear satisfaction of Merchant Saga and Maou Half World.

interpretation.reason: The reference is a changing live service and public sources do not expose a stable authoritative daily premium-currency budget.

acceptanceMatrix.condition: Canonical documents describe the reference target as experiential accessibility and cadence, not an unverifiable exact currency copy.
Ruby, character tickets, weapon tickets and pickup tickets have separate roles and server-authoritative ledgers.
Routine high-volume pulls are primarily ticket-funded; mandatory evolution is not forced to compete with hundreds of routine ruby pulls.
The first evolution is reachable without purchase or advertisement before its absence becomes a practical wall.
The free no-ad path covers 100% of mandatory core-roster evolution at the accepted pace.
Strong-new-game reset is the primary renewable free-ruby source and same-maximum repeat resets grant zero new ruby.
First-ten-minute, first-hour, first-seven-day and steady daily pull counts meet sealed ranges without deceptive presentation.
High draw volume supports x10, x50 and x100, skip, duplicate auto-conversion and no item-by-item disposal.
Each batch has a disclosed meaningful-progress floor; thousands of effectively zero-value pulls are rejected.
Character and weapon pity, pickup guarantee, carryover, exchange, duplicate caps and overflow are visible and statistically validated.
N and R retain endgame-relevant specialist, reset-start, low-cost or shop/delivery utility.
A base character or weapon performs its advertised role before duplicate skill upgrades.
First-reset, mature-reset and previous-maximum re-clear timing meet sealed satisfaction targets.
Reset restores automation, bulk purchase mode, known formation and known shop configuration where allowed.
Reset preview explicitly states lost, retained and earned state; ambiguous reset behavior is a hard failure.
Reward presentation creates frequent visible progress without covering combat or requiring prolonged opening sessions.
Optional ads stay within the sealed share of ruby and pulls; no-ad players remain on the target curve.
Ruby grants, reset rewards, ads, draws, duplicate conversion, pity and overflow are idempotent and replay-safe.
Simulation covers no-ad F2P, ad F2P, pass, controlled payer and stress personas across repeated resets and long-floor horizons.
Telemetry measures reward sources and outcomes with immutable audit IDs and privacy minimization.
Every user-owned decision is answered or its recommended default is explicitly accepted before canonical closure.
Independent critics attack reward cadence, monetization pressure, probability meaning, reset satisfaction, backend fraud and mobile density; unresolved P0/P1 equals zero.

failureConditions: Exact reference-game ruby parity is claimed without a measured reference window.
Routine high-volume pulls consume the same ruby budget needed for mandatory evolution.
A free no-ad core roster cannot afford mandatory evolution at target pace.
The first reset exceeds the accepted maximum or produces no obvious re-clear acceleration.
The same maximum floor can mint new ruby repeatedly.
Hundreds of pulls require item-by-item disposal or produce no visible progress.
Duplicate skill growth is uncapped or the base copy is functionally incomplete.
Forced advertisements become the dominant source of progress.
A user-owned decision is silently selected against the recorded recommendation.
Step 2 starts before the consolidated canonical and executable contract is sealed.
